question: A 28-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by ambulance after being hit in the head with a baseball bat. Physical examination shows swelling and bruising around the left temple and eye. A CT scan of the head shows a transverse fracture through the sphenoid bone and blood in the sphenoid sinus. Neurological examination is most likely to show which of the following findings?

options.opb: Inward deviation of the left eye
options.opd: Decreased hearing in the left ear
options.ope: Deviation of uvula to the right

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Trauma to the head -> transverse fracture through the sphenoid bone -> blood in the sphenoid sinus -> possible cranial nerve injury -> neurological examination findings. CHAIN: Trauma to the head -> sphenoid bone fracture -> blood in the sphenoid sinus -> cranial nerve compression -> neurological examination findings. CHAIN: Trauma to the head -> sphenoid bone fracture -> blood in the sphenoid sinus -> cranial nerve VII (facial nerve) involvement -> neurological examination findings. -> 85%
analysis: Based on the location of the fracture through the sphenoid bone and the presence of blood in the sphenoid sinus, the most likely neurological finding would be related to cranial nerve involvement.
